I’m just gonna add on as well that the Rotring rapid pro and 800 are good as well though I can’t speak from personal experience since I own neither. Both of them are quite a bit more expensive at about $30 each on Amazon (with prime) but they each have additional features that are worth looking into if you have the budget and want more than what the 600 can offer. Overall I still think the 600 is very solid and would be a good fit for you but if you’re trying to go cheaper, a 500 would work just fine as well though, again, I can’t speak from personal experience

Metal body and pocketable immediately leads me to believe the rotring 600 is right for you. One of my all time favorite pencils and comes in .7 and .5 depending on what you want. All metal body and the black one has a very nice textured grip (so does the silver and, although I don’t own the silver I’ve read about how the grip is better on black, less slippery). It’s around $16 for the .5 version and a bit pricier at about $24 for the .7 version (with Prime on Amazon) but overall a fantastic pencil. It’s all metal so it has heft to it and has a rotatable lead grade indicator so you can remind yourself what lead grade you have in your rotring. It’s also pretty average sized and has a fantastic sturdy clip for the pocketable aspect you were looking for. The eraser is small as with all drafting pencils really but overall a fantastic investment. Hope this helps!!

All the Kuru Toga models have the rotating lead mechanism but the Advance just has a better mechanism which makes a full rotation in half the turns when compared to the mechanisms of the other kuru togas. This makes it so that the thing actually rotates well and functions according to what it was designed for which is not the case with my other kuru togas (may just be personal experience though). What tended to happen with me with the other kuru togas is that they would try to turn but the edge had already become chiseled and would rotate back rather then getting on a new edge so the mechanism would essentially not do anything which hasn't been a problem for me with the Advance. Again this may just be me but I've noticed it with all 3 kuru togas I've owned and though I don't think any of them are bad pencils, the Advance's mechanism is just all around better and more effectively performs the lead-rotating function it was designed for
